newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian farmers happy with PM title talks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian farmers happy with PM title talks.

text.p: The National Farmers' Federation (NFF) was "very happy" with a preliminary round of talks with Prime Minister John Howard over native title issues, NFF president Don McGauchie said on Friday.
McGauchie was speaking with reporters after meeting Howard.
"The Prime Minister gave a very clear indication that he understands the difficulties the pastoral industry is in because of this decision," he said.
McGauchie was referring to a decision of Australia's High Court in December which ruled that pastoral leases and native title could co-exist.
McGauchie asked Howard to push through legislation to give pastoralists exclusive occupancy on their leases.
About 42 percent of Australia's land area is covered by pastoral leases and many mining leases are on pastoral leases.

Friday's meeting between the Prime Minister and the NFF is the first in a round of talks which Howard will hold in the next week or so, when he is scheduled to meet with Australia's mining interests and Aboriginal groups.
McGauchie said he was optimistic that a conclusion could be reached on the problem.
It would take some work to produce this but an answer was wanted as soon as possible, he said.
"We agreed with the Prime Minister that while we want a quick solution, we don't want a quickie solution," he said.
"Nineteen ninety seven has to be the year in which we fix it," he said.

McGauchie said he asked Howard for the government to fund pastoralists and native title claimants on an equal basis in any legal actions. "He showed a great deal of sympathy with our position," he said.
